B: an arbitrary real n by n orthogonal matrix used in the determinant-parity argument
Q: the real n by n orthogonal matrix in the theorem
u: the real unit column vector in the theorem
v: a real n-dimensional column vector used in the fixed-vector hypothesis
w: the constructed nonzero real n-dimensional column vector fixed by HQ
z: a nonzero complex eigenvector of B associated with lambda
x: an arbitrary vector used to prove that I-Q is injective
y: an arbitrary vector used to prove that I-Q is injective
r: the total algebraic multiplicity of the real eigenvalues of B
n: a positive integer, the dimension of the real vector space and the matrix size
I: the n by n identity matrix
x^{\\mathsf T}: the transpose of a real vector x
u^\\perp: the subspace of real vectors orthogonal to u
z^*: the conjugate transpose of the complex vector z
